slide_title: Relationship Between Observed Phenotype and F2 Offspring
original_text: Relationship Between Observed Phenotype and F2 Offspring
explanation: The relationship between observed phenotype and F2 offspring demonstrates that the dominant phenotype may hide a recessive allele, meaning that individuals showing the dominant phenotype can be either homozygous dominant or heterozygous.

questions.q: Why can we not always determine an individual's genotype just by looking at their dominant phenotype?
opts: The recessive allele is always destroyed.
The dominant allele masks the expression of the recessive allele in heterozygotes.
Mutated alleles do not align on the chromosomes.
questions.exp: Option B is correct because heterozygous individuals (Aa) carry a recessive allele but exhibit the dominant phenotype, making them indistinguishable from homozygous dominant individuals (AA) by phenotype alone.
